intro: Here in Bartın province, the walls of Amasra Castle wrap the headland between two bays and the island opposite, their present story reaching back to the 9th century. Genoese coats of arms still sit above its gates, and a neighbourhood lives inside it to this day.
history: The walls go back to Roman foundations, but they owe most of their present form to a Byzantine rebuilding in the 9th century; later, the Genoese repaired them. They enclose the headland between two bays and the island of Boztepe opposite, and the bridge between them is still in use. Genoese coats of arms sit above the gates, and inside the circuit a neighbourhood still lives.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Genoese arms and the Kemere bridge; then follow the Boztepe walls, and look for the Kuşkayası road monument.
facts: Did you know? The neighbourhood inside the walls makes this one of the few cases in Türkiye of a medieval castle inhabited without a break. And above the castle gates, Genoese coats of arms still sit.
outro: This brings our tour of Amasra Castle to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you, and remember that people still call these walls home. Enjoy your visit.
